function.text: Each muscle is wrapped in a sheath of dense, irregular connective tissue called the epimysium,
muscle fibers are organized into individual bundles, each called a fascicle, by a middle layer of connective tissue called the perimysium.
each muscle fiber is encased in a thin connective tissue layer of collagen and reticular fibers called the endomysium.

Where C:F is independent of fibre size and a reduction in this parameter is indicative of capillary rarefaction (assuming fibre number is not changed), CD is influenced by fibre size and is a reflection of the diffusion capacity of the capillary bed of the muscle tissue.
The plasma membrane of muscle fibers is called the sarcolemma,

structures.name: Myonuclei

function.text: Multiple nuclei mean multiple copies of genes.

structures.note: Number and spacing are illustrative: no myonuclear data were reported by Fitts or Trappe.

structures.name: Mitochondria

function.text: The filamentous mitochondria (m) predominately encircling I bands in pre-flight muscle fibres become more globular post-flight and invade the A bands, most striking with greater atrophy

structures.note: Qualitative electron-microscopy description; number, size and volume fraction are illustrative.

function.text: the specialized smooth endoplasmic reticulum, which stores, releases, and retrieves calcium ions (Ca++).

structures.name: T-tubule and triad

function.text: The T-tubules carry the action potential into the interior of the cell.

structures.note: Triad: 'The close association of one T-tubule with two terminal cisternae on both sides of the tubule forms the triad' (Al-Qusairi & Laporte 2011, Introduction).

function.text: The contraction of a striated muscle fiber occurs as the sarcomeres, linearly arranged within myofibrils, shorten as myosin heads pull on the actin filaments.
Thin filaments, anchored at their ends by the Z-discs, do not extend completely into the central region of the sarcomere
a central region that only contains thick filaments, anchored at their bases at a spot called the M-line.
The region where thick and thin filaments overlap has a dense appearance, as there is little space between the filaments.
When a sarcomere contracts, the Z lines move closer together, and the I band becomes smaller.
each thick filament of roughly 300 myosin molecules has multiple myosin heads
After prolonged spaceflight, thin filament length increases (indicated by red extensions of thin filaments) and density increases in the Near M region (post-flight).

structures.name: Titin

function.text: regarding the thick filaments, titin seems to act as a molecular ruler or template as it directly regulates the thick filament length.

structures.note: Drawn schematically from the Z-disc to the M-line; no titin data were reported by Fitts or Trappe.

structures.name: Tibia and fibula (origin of the soleus)

function.text: It originates in the superior tibia, fibula, and interosseous membrane.

structures.note: Kenhub: 'The soleus muscle arises from the soleal line on the dorsal surface of the tibia' and 'Part of the fibers arises from the tendinous arch of the soleus'. Bone shapes are illustrative.

structures.name: Calcaneal (Achilles) tendon and calcaneus

function.text: The superficial muscles in the posterior compartment of the leg all insert onto the calcaneal tendon, a strong tendon that inserts into the calcaneal bone of the ankle.

structures.note: Kenhub: 'together they insert onto the posterior surface of the calcaneus via the calcaneal tendon'.

illustrative.name: Leg, bone, tendon and skin shapes
illustrative.reason: Procedural shapes placed to follow the described origins and insertion; not traced from any image. Only the soleus and gastrocnemius volumes and the shank length come from data.

illustrative.name: Soleus outline
illustrative.reason: Procedural shape. Its absolute volume is scaled to the reported mean (455 cm³ preflight); the outline itself is not from imaging of the crew.

illustrative.name: Fascicles drawn in the cross-section
illustrative.reason: The real number of fascicles in a soleus section was not measured in these studies. Fascicles are drawn as a representative mosaic.

illustrative.name: Fibres drawn in the fascicle
illustrative.reason: A representative bundle. Fibre diameters and the share of each fibre type come from data; the count and positions do not.

illustrative.name: Capillary positions
illustrative.reason: About 1.8 capillaries per type I fibre (Hendrickse et al. 2022 baseline) are placed in the gaps between fibres; positions are illustrative.

illustrative.name: Myofibrils drawn in the fibre (preflight)
illustrative.reason: A real 98 µm fibre holds thousands of 1.2 µm myofibrils; a reduced number is drawn at the true diameter. During the mission the count is scaled with fibre cross-sectional area (approximation).

illustrative.name: Myonuclei drawn on the fibre
illustrative.reason: Number and spacing of myonuclei were not measured in these studies.

illustrative.name: Mitochondria drawn in the fibre
illustrative.reason: No mitochondrial volume fraction was measured; size and number are chosen to be visible at this scale. Shape follows the qualitative EM description (filamentous around the I band preflight; globular, invading the A band after flight in crew with high atrophy).

illustrative.name: Thick filaments drawn in the lattice cross-section
illustrative.reason: A small hexagonal patch at the normalised 31.3 nm spacing. The number of thin filaments per thick filament comes from the reported ratio; their exact positions are illustrative.

illustrative.name: Thin-filament lengths in the longitudinal view
illustrative.reason: Following the concept in Fitts et al. Fig. 16: thin filaments have different lengths; the share long enough to reach the near-M region is calculated from the reported densities (density near M ÷ 3251 μm−2).

qualitative_findings.location: PDF page 13, Results 'Ultrastructural changes and quantification'
qualitative_findings.quote: crew members exhibiting high levels of slow fibre atrophy in the soleus muscle following 6 months of spaceflight had smaller myofibrils, fewer intracellular lipids, smaller and globular mitochondria and increased space between myofibrils filled with glycogen particles (Fig. 10).
qualitative_findings.applies_to: Crew with high fibre atrophy (for example subject F, 51 % atrophy). Not a group mean; not quantified.

qualitative_findings.quote: subjects with little atrophy retained similar sized, closely packed myofibrils, lipid droplets and filamentous mitochondria encircling the myofibrils at the I band level (Fig. 10).
the two crew members with the greatest soleus type I fibre atrophy also lost the most soleus muscle volume detected by MRI.
qualitative_findings.applies_to: Why fibre and whole-muscle changes are shown side by side: the fibre CSA loss (biopsy, R+0) is larger than the whole-muscle volume loss (MRI, R+4). The page does not reconcile them.

spaceflight_cohorts.label: Spaceflight cohorts (front-loaded, then level)
spaceflight_cohorts.method: duration_model.normalized_shape('soleus_volume', 177): the existing multi-cohort soleus curve (LeBlanc et al. 2000 plus the 8-day point in register entry E1), divided by its own plateau so it runs from 0 at launch to 1 at day 177. Only its shape is used; every parameter is scaled to its own Fitts or Trappe endpoints.

supporting_quotes.quote: The composite data from Skylab, MIR and Shuttle flights suggest that the loss of limb muscle mass is exponential with the duration of flight, and that a microgravity steady state may be reached by approximately 180 days (Fitts et al. 2000).

A linear regression of the percent loss against flight duration showed no significant slope for any of the regions, suggesting that the volume changes reached a new steady state by or before ~4 mo of flight.

spaceflight_cohorts.assumed: All parameters follow the same time course as soleus volume in separate Shuttle and Mir crews: about 38 % of the end-of-mission change by day 8, 58 % by day 17 and the full change from day 115 on, joined by straight segments.
spaceflight_cohorts.why: These are the only spaceflight measurements of the soleus at more than one mission length. Fitts et al. and LeBlanc et al. both describe a loss that slows and levels off.
spaceflight_cohorts.needed_to_replace: Repeated in-flight measurements (for example MRI or ultrasound) of the same crew during a six-month mission.
spaceflight_cohorts.notice: In-between days are an approximation. No one measured these crew members during flight. The curve borrows its shape from other crews (Space Shuttle and Mir, 8 to 197 days), who exercised differently, and is scaled to this cohort's own before and after values.

linear.label: Straight line (constant daily rate)

supporting_quotes.quote: Across all muscles except the rectus femoris (no change), there was a linear decline during bed rest, with the highest atrophic rate occurring in the soleus (–0.33%/d).
Model R 2 , AIC, and BIC for the linear models was similar to the exponential decay and fractional polynomial nonlinear models

linear.assumed: Every parameter changes by the same amount each day, from its preflight value at launch to its end-of-mission value at day 177.
linear.why: In a 70-day bed-rest study without exercise (a ground analogue, not spaceflight), soleus size fell along a straight line and showed no plateau. Its rate (−0.33 %/day) is NOT used: it would predict far more loss than the crew showed. Only the straight shape is borrowed.
linear.needed_to_replace: Repeated in-flight measurements of the same crew.
linear.notice: In-between days are an approximation that assumes an even daily rate. The straight shape comes from a bed-rest study (people lying in bed on the ground, no exercise), not from spaceflight.

check_points.quote: The 20 and 35% decline in the slow type I fibre diameter and force observed in this work exceeded the 8 and 21% drop in these variables following a 17-day Shuttle flight (Widrick et al. 1999)
check_points.note: A different crew (four Shuttle astronauts, 17-day flight). Shown for comparison only; not used to build the curve.

check_points.quote: exceeded the 8 and 21% drop in these variables following a 17-day Shuttle flight (Widrick et al. 1999)

the cross-sectional areas (CSAs) of the slow type I and fast type IIa fibres of the soleus muscles of the four crew members were on average 15 and 26% smaller post- compared to pre-flight (Widrick et al. 1999).

context.quote: After just 6 days of bed rest, fibre atrophy (−23.2 ± 12.4%, P < 0.001) and reductions in capillary‐to‐fibre ratio (C:F; 1.97 ± 0.57 vs . 1.56 ± 0.41, P < 0.001) were proportional in both muscles
context.use: Context only: in bed rest, fibre atrophy was fast in the first week and slower afterwards. Not used in any calculation.
